- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; reduce subsequent forecast by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days falling from peak), model often fails to adjust; apply downward bias of 1–4% for next 2–3 periods.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 periods if sentiment changes abruptly.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model often misaligns with true trend; align forecast with sentiment average over 3-period window.
